e-4949.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(4,8,2).$ Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 6 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14060274/assets/0589ebbdb2c14b93e1296b9e1f8b0caa0c3df49bff4c9fbb97e4c18102844ec1.png)

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 2+6\cdot 4+4\cdot (-4)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-2+24-16|}{\sqrt{4+16+16}} \\  & =\frac{|\,6\,|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

e-4950.problem: Given that $Q(1,-2,-1)$ lies on the plane $\Pi:\mathbf{r} \cdot \langle 2, 0, -2 \rangle = 4,$ find the shortest distance from $P(0 , -1 , 2)$ to $\Pi.$
e-4950.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,-2,-1⟩-⟨0,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $\mathbf{n}= \langle 2, 0, -2 \rangle.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+0+6|}{\sqrt{4+0+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,8\,|}{\sqrt{8}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

e-4951.knowledge_point: Finding the Shortest Distance Between a Point and a Plane Given in Cartesian Form
e-4951.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(3 , -10 , 3)$ and the plane $\Pi$ with equation $2x+y-2z = -1$.
e-4951.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=4$ and $y=-5$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+y-2z & =-1 \\ 2(4)+(-5)+1 & =2z \\ 4 & =2z \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(4, -5, 2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overrightarrow{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨4,-5,2⟩-⟨3,-10,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1,5,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $\mathbf{n}=\langle a,b,c \rangle.$ So, for the plane $\Pi,$ we have $\mathbf{n}= \langle 2, 1, -2 \rangle.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot 2+5\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+5+2|}{\sqrt{4+1+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,9\,|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(1,-5,3).$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,-5,3⟩-⟨-1,2,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-7,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨1,0,4⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|2\cdot 1+(-7)\cdot 0+6\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+0+24|}{\sqrt{1+16}} \\  & =\frac{|26|}{\sqrt{17}} \\  & =\frac{26\sqrt{17}}{17}\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(2,-1,1).$ Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-3)\cdot 4+(-3)\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-12-6-4|}{\sqrt{16+4+16}} \\  & =\frac{|-22|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{11}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Given that $Q(4,-2,8)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-3,6,2⟩=-8$, find the shortest distance from $P(3,-4,2)$ to $Π.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨4,-2,8⟩-⟨3,-4,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,2,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-3,6,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot (-3)+2\cdot 6+6\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-3+12+12|}{\sqrt{9+36+4}} \\  & =\frac{|21|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{21}{7} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Given that $Q(1,3,4)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-4,2,0⟩=2$, find the shortest distance from $P(5,-2,3)$ to $Π.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,3,4⟩-⟨5,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-4,2,0⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-4)\cdot (-4)+5\cdot 2+1\cdot 0|}{\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|16+10+0|}{\sqrt{16+4+0}} \\  & =\frac{|26|}{\sqrt{20}} \\  & =\frac{13\sqrt{5}}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-2$ and $y=1$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+2y+2z & =8 \\ -1(-2)+2(1)+2z & =8 \\ 2z & =4 \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-2,1,2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-2,1,2⟩-⟨-2,3,-6⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-2,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-1,2,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|0\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 2+8\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|0-4+16|}{\sqrt{1+4+4}} \\  & =\frac{|12|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{12}{3} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
